newsitem.title: UK: Horse racing-Make A Stand in record-breaking Champion victory.
newsitem.headline: Horse racing-Make A Stand in record-breaking Champion victory.

text.p: CHELTENHAM, England, March 11 - Trailblazing handicapper Make A Stand led from pillar to post on Tuesday to win the Champion Hurdle in record-breaking time on the first day of the Cheltenham jump racing Festival.

Jumping superbly on the lightning fast ground, the 7-1 shot ridden by Tony McCoy ran out an effortless five lengths winner up the tough Cheltenham Hill from the 33-1 Irish outsider Theatreworld and the 9-2 chance Space Trucker, another Irish challenger.
"What a fantastic performance out there in front," said trainer Martin Pipe, landing his second Champion Hurdle after winning in 1993 with Granville Again.
McCoy, only recently back in action after fracturing a shoulder and collar bone, was breathless with admiration after the six year old had galloped his 16 rivals into the ground.
The Irishman said: : "It was great to make all the running like that. He was certainly there to be shot at."

Make A Stand, the first Champion Hurdle winner to lead all the way since Night Nurse triumphed in 1977, adopted the bold front running tactics that won him three valuable handicaps earlier in the season and never looked like being caught as he made the progression to the top class with comfort.

But the race was full of shocks with last year's winner Collier Bay, clearly ill at ease on the fast ground, being pulled up and the hotly fancied 7-2 favourite Large Action apparently breaking down at the second hurdle where jockey Jamie Osborne had to hastily dismount.

Make A Stand barely out of the novice class, had Pipe nearly lost for words after the race "Didn't he jump along super," he told reporters of what could prove an expensive victory for the prolific trainer.
For Pipe had promised his son David a new car if Make A Stand could land the Champion Hurdle.

"I think I've lost all my prize money, " the trainer quipped. But he didn't dare celebrate until Make A Stand had forged his way up the stamina-sapping Cheltenham Hill without showing any signs of weakening.
"I was worried but then the sticks (whips) were flying with all the jockeys behind him," he said.

Pipe and McCoy were in unbeatable form as the two also combined to win the Arkle Challenge Trophy with the French Import Or Royal, whose passage to victory was made easier when hot favourite Mulligan capsized at the last open ditch.

Earlier, jockey Osborne, leading winner back in 1992 at jumping's most famous festival, started the meeting off in magnificent style when steering Shadow Leader to a 10 lengths victory in the Supreme Novices Hurdle.
